newsitem.title: JAPAN: Japan bank sector shares up but off highs in Tokyo.
newsitem.headline: Japan bank sector shares up but off highs in Tokyo.

text.p: Shares in the Japanese banking sector soared in Tokyo on Thursday but by mid-afternoon were off earlier peaks.
The rise was partly due to market hopes that the government would use public money to buy collateralised land formerly owned by troubled financial firms.

A front-page report in Thursday's edition of business daily Nihon Keizai Shimbun that the government plans to use more public funds to buy collateralised land previously owned by failed "jusen" mortgage firms and other troubled financial firms helped push up Tokyo share prices on Thursday morning.

A Finance Ministry official told Reuters on Thursday that the government was mulling the use of budget money already set aside in the 1997/98 state budget for such land purchases, but added that it was not considering allocating fresh public money for such use.
As of 0419 GMT, shares in Sakura Bank Ltd were up 41 yen at 737 yen with a turnover of 8.08 million shares, the fifth-heaviest volume on the first section of the Tokyo Stock Exchange.
By 0513 GMT shares of Fuji Bank Ltd had risen 70 yen to 1,350 yen. Turnover was 7.80 million shares.
Reports of possible government land purchases provided support to Japanese banks, which have been unable to dispose of collateralised properties due to the sluggish real estate market.
